why: Avro Vulcan B.2 flight-deck canopy: mostly metal, a smooth fairing blended into the dorsal hump (the model's own mould line, the envelope of its frame lumps), with small thick heavily framed windows. Descriptions of the B.2 give a five-panel windscreen with its framing and small round side windows; pilots complained about the view; no roof (eyebrow) windows were found. Flat panes here: one small pane in front of each pilot on the windscreen's flat raked plane (y = Y_B + K (Z_B - z), independent of x; a broad metal centre structure and a centre rib between them), one small quarter pane each side on the flat vertical side facet beside it (the plane x = XF), and one small round side window each side (a 16-gon in the plane x = x0 + sl (y - yc), tangent to the fairing). The pane layout and sizes (and the fifth windscreen panel of the description) are not documented with dimensions, so they are the model's own line and UNVERIFIED against the real jet (see canopy_vulcan_b2.py). The rear crew compartment has no windows and no glass.
